tagline: Climb through changing forests to lakes, red hoodoos and Mount Nebo
intro: Nebo Loop winds between Payson and Nephi through the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. The climb starts among scrub oak, passes maples and quaking aspens, then reaches fir, Engelmann spruce and lodgepole pine before descending to the other valley. The Forest Service identifies it as a National Scenic Byway and highlights overlooks of Utah Valley and Mount Nebo, alongside red sandstone formations. The archived federal guide allows an hour for a one-way drive or a day to explore.

The byway also helped preserve a landmark at its Payson end. Peteetneet School, built in 1901, faced demolition in 1989. People Preserving Peteetneet helped save and restore it; its location on the scenic byway brought more than $100,000 in Utah Department of Transportation restoration funding. The school became a museum and civic center.

From Payson, 600 East becomes Nebo Loop Road, Forest Road 15, into the mountains. Payson Lakes lie 12 miles south of town. The route links the lakes, a Mount Nebo overlook and Devils Kitchen’s red hoodoos before reaching SR 132 east of Nephi. That junction is five miles from I-15. At the Utah Valley overlook, canyons frame the view toward the lake below, as ranger George Garcia describes it in Visit Utah’s account.

moments.title: Payson Lakes
moments.text: Payson Lakes offer a paved walk beside the water, 12 miles south of Payson. In Visit Utah’s account, Forest Service public affairs officer Loyal Clark describes the reconstruction of the paved nature path beside the lake. Three lakes provide fishing, swimming and boating; Visit Utah lists brook and rainbow trout among the fish here. The Forest Service also identifies improved picnic areas and camping at the recreation area.
moments.notice: A paved nature path follows the lake.

moments.title: Mount Nebo
moments.text: Mount Nebo has two summits, and the record of which one is higher changed with a new survey. Early surveys favored the southern summit; a resurvey in the 1970s established that the northern summit was higher. Nebo is the highest mountain in the Wasatch Range and the centerpiece of the Mount Nebo Wilderness. Visit Utah identifies a Mount Nebo overlook along the byway. Separate trails reach the two summits: the south summit has approaches from east or west, while the north summit trail starts northeast of the mountain. Its name comes from the biblical Mount Nebo in Jordan.

moments.title: Devils Kitchen
moments.text: Red sandstone interrupts the mountain greenery at Devils Kitchen. The Forest Service describes an eroded formation with red rock hoodoos, reached by a half-mile round-trip trail. A paved trail and observation deck give this geologic interest site its viewing places, and picnic facilities are provided. Visit Utah compares the formation to Bryce Canyon; the Forest Service emphasizes the red color against the greenery along the rest of the byway.
moments.notice: Red sandstone formations contrast with the mountain greenery.

practical: Payson Lakes: Nebo Loop Road closes in winter. (checked 2026-10-11)
